world 2 (key covert).reader_note: "through a church charity that did not name its source" gives covert away; also the passage never says the ministry is national.

world 3 (key crude).reader_note: Crude needs the fixed sum regardless of damage plus the unfilled sandbags; 'acted within a day' kills complacent, but bureaucratic is a defensible reading of one-size-fits-all.

world 0 (key bureaucratic).reader_note: "a separate claim for each room ... came back unread if one box was blank" gives bureaucratic outright.

world 1 (key complacent).reader_note: Freak-event judgment on past record plus minimal repair gives complacent; bureaucratic is a plausible near-miss.

world 1 (key cloned).reader_note: "built three new hospitals ... from the stone building's floor plan, staffed each with its number of nurses" is the definition of cloned; "went on as before" kills cannibalized.

world 2 (key bartered).reader_note: Bartered requires joining 'no payment received' with 'that same month the university's plot passed to the board'; cannibalized is a tempting near-miss.

world 0 (key cannibalized).reader_note: 'X-ray machine, its operating tables, and most of its surgeons were moved to the city one by one, as the new building needed them' gives cannibalized alone.

world 2 (key courier).reader_note: "sealed packet he never opened" and "corrected alone" kill confidant and critic; the carrying sentence gives courier.

world 3 (key critic).reader_note: Easy: 'reviewed each of her books... naming the weak lines and the forced rhymes' literally describes a critic.

world 0 (key benefactor).reader_note: "he paid off its debts and sent her a fixed sum every month" gives benefactor outright.

world 1 (key confidant).reader_note: 'The letters ... held what her diaries and her other letters leave out' plus 'He told no one' is the definition of confidant.

world 0 (key cornered).reader_note: "could buy grain from no one else, and ... paid whatever price the house named" defines cornered.

world 1 (key bankrolled).reader_note: 'the forty small dealers... borrowed from it' gives bankrolled; 'never bought or sold a sack of grain itself' kills cornered.

world 2 (key coordinated).reader_note: Set days, shared warehouse and single convoy give coordinated; "never bought or sold a sack" and "every dealer still set his own prices" kill cornered.

world 3 (key ambassador).reader_note: The spring-visits sentence gives ambassador; apprentice is a literal lure from "technician ... hired straight out of high school".

world 0 (key apprentice).reader_note: The third sentence (he corrected her hands until she could work without him, then she took over using his methods) carries apprentice alone; distractors are not near-misses.

world 2 (key accomplice).reader_note: 'copied every notebook out afresh with figures that matched his papers and emptied the remaining samples down the drain' gives accomplice alone.

world 1 (key accessible).reader_note: "ramps at every door ... shelves stood open to anyone who walked in" gives accessible away.

world 2 (key adaptable).reader_note: Easy: 'no fixed walls... shelves ran on floor tracks... partitions hung from ceiling rails' says adaptable outright.

world 3 (key airy).reader_note: "The outer walls were glass from floor to ceiling ... the staff switched on no lamps" gives airy; murals and trees kill austere.

world 0 (key austere).reader_note: 'bare concrete ... plain rows of bulbs ... struck every carving, mural, and carpet' gives austere; 'low reading rooms' kills airy.

world 0 (key checkpoint).reader_note: Stop, list, seal, refuse weapons reads as checkpoint, but the neutral-trust setup (neither lord trusted the other) makes broker defensible.

world 1 (key broker).reader_note: 'carried each lord's offers over the pass and back, proposed terms' gives broker in one sentence.

world 2 (key custodian).reader_note: "sealed each family's goods ... handed them back ... with the seals unbroken" gives custodian; checkpoint literally sits on the pass.

world 3 (key counterweight).reader_note: Land, western-elected abbots, and bishop's support kept the eastern lord short: counterweight; checkpoint is a location-based lure.

world 0 (key braided).reader_note: Easy: 'the two lines cross and recross' is a literal description of braiding; 'note for note from start to finish' kills clipped.

world 1 (key clipped).reader_note: "The composer kept only the first eight bars" of thirty-two gives clipped outright.
